title: Senior Product Manager, Verticals
description:
At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.

Lyft connects people to transportation to change the way we live and get around our communities. We are looking for product managers who bring exceptional creative and analytical skills to drive forward a best in class product. Product management at Lyft leads the integration of engineering, data science, and design to achieve the company's vision for reinventing transportation. We are looking for entrepreneurial and passionate Product Managers to innovate and execute across a rapidly growing, fast paced company and industry from our San Francisco headquarters.

Lyft's Verticals team owns three of the most strategically important and operationally complex marketplaces in our business: airports, scheduled rides, and events. These are the moments that matter most. Airports are a defining touchpoint in the Lyft experience: high-stakes, high-complexity, and critical to both rider trust and driver earnings. Scheduled rides give riders confidence and control while giving drivers greater predictability. Events, from packed stadium concerts to sold-out games, require precision logistics and seamless coordination at scale. Together, these verticals represent some of the highest-intent, highest-value use cases on the Lyft platform.

As a Senior Product Manager on the Verticals team, you'll lead a cross-functional team to shape how millions of people plan, book, and experience their journeys across these critical moments. You'll build seamless booking flows, deeply personalized experiences, and robust integrations with travel and event partners. You'll also take on some of the most complex challenges in rideshare: optimizing rider-driver matching in dynamic, high-variability environments, advancing demand forecasting, improving real-time driver guidance, and designing targeted incentives that drive growth. The solutions you build need to work everywhere, from a quiet regional airport to JFK, and from a Tuesday morning scheduled ride to 60,000 fans leaving a stadium at once.

Responsibilities:

• Understand Lyft's strategic and competitive position. Set goals and success metrics that align with Lyft's mission and drive maximum impact based on data analysis, market research, and usability studies

• Set an incredibly ambitious vision that motivates and inspires your team, peers, and leadership, and that accounts for the distinct dynamics of airports, scheduled rides, and events

• Completely own your team's products, existing or new, from ideation through development, experimentation, launch, growth, and maintenance, caring deeply about both rider and driver experiences

• Lead and align cross-functional partners, including engineers, designers, data scientists, analysts, marketers, business partners, and operations, to drive a shared vision

• Communicate clear roadmaps, priorities, experiments, and decisions across a wide spectrum of audiences from partner teams to executive leadership

Experience:

• 6+ years of experience in product management, product design, or equivalent consulting experience with significant time spent leading consumer mobile apps or marketplace products

• Experience working with or alongside data science and operations teams on complex products; familiarity with experimentation, marketplace dynamics, or logistics is a plus

• Passion for Lyft and what we are trying to achieve in sustainable urban transportation

• Natural ability to make things happen around you. You manage project ambiguity, complexity, and interdependencies in an organized and structured way

• Strong ability to define and analyze metrics that inform the success of products and the health of the business

• Excellent judgment and thoughtfulness about the dynamics of a product ecosystem, including balancing the needs of riders and drivers

title: Senior User Researcher
description:
At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset - who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.

As a Senior User Researcher at Snowflake, you’ll shape what we build and how customers experience it. You’ll work alongside product, design, engineering, and marketing leads to set priorities, make tough calls, and bring ideas to market. Your deep understanding of customer needs and business goals will make you a trusted partner in those decisions.

This role calls for deep research craft, strong business judgment, and fluency with AI. You’ll know when to move quickly, when to dig deeper, and how to turn what you learn into better outcomes for Snowflake’s customers.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Partner with product, design, engineering, and marketing leads to set priorities that make a meaningful difference for Snowflake’s customers.

- Become an expert on your customers’ needs and goals, your product area, and the business objectives your team is working toward.

- Lead qualitative and quantitative research, choosing the methods and level of rigor each decision demands.

- Make product and go-to-market decisions alongside your partners. Work through tradeoffs, build alignment, and carry decisions through launch and adoption.

- Combine customer research, product usage data, and prior findings to identify opportunities and understand what needs to change.

- Identify where AI can strengthen your research, apply it deliberately, and hold the results to a high standard.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

- 5+ years of industry user research experience, with examples of decisions that changed because of your work and the customer or business outcomes that followed.

- Deep experience across qualitative and quantitative methods. You can explain how you chose an approach, what its limits were, and why the evidence was sufficient for the decision.

- A track record of earning the trust of cross-functional leads and working with them through difficult product or go-to-market tradeoffs.

- Experience connecting customer needs to product and business goals, including identifying opportunities that weren’t apparent from the initial question.

- Experience using product usage data alongside primary research to reach a more complete understanding of a problem.

- Examples of AI applications you’ve put into practice in your research work-and the judgment you used to decide where they belonged.

Every Snowflake employee is expected to follow the company’s confidentiality and security standards for handling sensitive data. Snowflake employees must abide by the company’s data security plan as an essential part of their duties. It is every employee's duty to keep customer information secure and confidential.

Snowflake is growing fast, and we’re scaling our team to help enable and accelerate our growth. We are looking for people who share our values, challenge ordinary thinking, and push the pace of innovation while building a future for themselves and Snowflake.

How do you want to make your impact?

description:
ABOUT BABBEL LABS

Babbel Labs is building the future of language learning. We are an AI-first, independent company within the Babbel group, based in Berlin. Our teams bring AI, research and product together to ship experiences that set a new standard for how people learn.

THE ROLE

We're a small, fast-moving team rethinking how people learn languages with AI. We're looking for an experienced product designer to take over hands-on design leadership: shaping the product's direction, running discovery, and getting work delivered.

This is a design leadership and mentoring role, not a people management role. You'll guide the craft and direction of the design team. Speed, precision and quality are how we work. You'll set the pace. You'll work AI-first, using various ways to test ideas quickly and turning the best ones into experiences that are ready to hand off.

HOW YOU'LL MAKE AN IMPACT

- Lead design across discovery and delivery, owning key design decisions for AI-first language learning experiences.

- Design AI-powered learning experiences. Shape how learners interact with AI, from conversation and voice to feedback that stays clear and trustworthy even when the AI gets things wrong.

- Work as an AI builder. Use AI tools first to speed up research, exploring ideas, prototyping and delivery.

- Prototype in code. Build prototypes in SwiftUI and HTML to test ideas and produce vision prototypes that are ready to hand off.

- Design with Claude Code and Figma together. Figma is one tool among several here, not where every project starts.

- Coach and mentor the small, experienced design team, who also work as AI builders, and help them share one set of AI-first design principles.

- Work across disciplines with engineers, product managers, linguists and language learning specialists.

YOUR SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS

- Proven design leadership. Solid experience leading product design, with a record of shipping work that users actually adopted.

- Excellent UI craft and motion design. Learning happens moment by moment, so polished interfaces and purposeful motion are essential to a great learning experience.

- Hands-on prototyping in code. You're comfortable in SwiftUI and HTML/CSS/JS and can build things people can use and test.

- AI fluency. You use AI tools like Claude Code as a real part of how you design, not an add-on.

- Design systems know-how. A working knowledge of design systems and how they make teams faster and more consistent.

- A coaching mindset. Experience coaching designers and raising a team's standards through example, feedback and shared practices.

- Clear communication. You work well with technical and non-technical partners, including specialists like linguists and learning designers.

- Comfort with ambiguity. You thrive on fast iteration and figuring things out as you go.

WHAT YOU'LL GET

- Room to learn new tools as they arrive. Try them on real work as soon as they come out, and help decide what the team adopts.

- A consumer product used around the world. Design for a live product that real learners use every day, globally.

- A competitive salary. Salary range: TBD. Pay that reflects the level of the role and the impact you'll have on the product and the team.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

- Delivery-ready prototypes. Prototypes that give engineering and stakeholders a clear vision to build from.

- Faster, better design work. Quality and speed improve through AI tools and design systems.

- An aligned design team. A team that is coached, confident and aligned on AI-first design principles.

WAYS OF WORKING

This is a hands-on design leadership role on a small, experienced design team that works AI-first. AI tools are built into how the whole team works every day, from discovery to delivery. It is hybrid: a mix of time together in the office and working remotely.

title: Recruitment Lead
description:

London | Full-time | Hybrid | Shoreditch/Liverpool Street

WE’RE MAKING TRAVEL EFFORTLESS. JOIN US.

Travel is essential, whether it’s visiting family, starting a new adventure, or taking a career defining trip. Yet today, over 4 billion airline passengers rely on tech that hasn't changed in decades.

At Duffel, we’re rebuilding the infrastructure underpinning the global travel industry. Backed by top-tier investors (Benchmark, Blossom, Index Ventures, and Kima Ventures) and born out of Y Combinator (S18), we’re simplifying complex systems to build the future of travel.

- Manage a team of recruiters setting workload priorities, running 1:1s, keeping a pulse on pipelines, and supporting their development

- Partner closely with leaders on recruitment strategy and delivery across all functions, with a particular focus on scaling technical hiring

- Maintain and improve a structured interview infrastructure so the whole team runs a consistent, high-signal process

- A champion of clean data and documentation: from interview guides to Ashby set-up (Jobs and Openings, sources, archive reasons). You keep Ashby accurate enough that leaders trust the numbers.

- Excellent stakeholder management: comfortable pushing back on hiring managers and execs with evidence when the plan or process needs it, in a fast-moving, collaborative environment.

title: Principal Technical Product Manager, Catalysis
description:
ABOUT SANDBOXAQ

SandboxAQ is a high-growth company delivering AI solutions that address some of the world's greatest challenges. The company’s Large Quantitative Models (LQMs) power advances in life sciences, financial services, navigation, cybersecurity, and other sectors.

We are a global team that is tech-focused and includes experts in AI, chemistry, cybersecurity, physics, mathematics, medicine, engineering, and other specialties. The company emerged from Alphabet Inc. as an independent, growth capital-backed company in 2022, funded by leading investors and supported by a braintrust of industry leaders.

At SandboxAQ, we’ve cultivated an environment that encourages creativity, collaboration, and impact. By investing deeply in our people, we’re building a thriving, global workforce poised to tackle the world's epic challenges. Join us to advance your career in pursuit of an inspiring mission, in a community of like-minded people who value entrepreneurialism, ownership, and transformative impact.

THE OPPORTUNITY

SandboxAQ’s AI Simulation (AISim) division develops and applies Large Quantitative Models (LQMs) that are grounded in physics, chemistry, mathematics and biology to simulate molecular behavior with scientific precision and accelerate discovery in the physical world across biopharma, chemicals, advanced materials, healthcare, and so much more.

Within AISim, ChemSim is SandboxAQ's AI-driven materials discovery platform. We are seeking an exceptional Product Manager to own the Catalysis vertical. This is a dual-mandate role. In the near term, you will be the product owner for catalysis within SandboxAQ's $500M CHIPS Act R&D award from the U.S. Department of Commerce, translating contractual objectives into product requirements and external fulfilment, whilst partnering with Program Managers to ensure successful milestone delivery. In parallel, you will build the commercial foundation that turns catalysis from a government-funded R&D workstream into a product-led business generating durable, recurring revenue from the broader materials and process-chemistry market.

Catalysis is one of the largest and most consequential application areas in applied chemistry. It underpins refining and downstream oil and gas, commodity and petrochemical production, emissions control, and the energy transition (hydrogen electrolysis, carbon utilization, e-fuels and chemical recycling etc) alongside semiconductor process chemistry and fine chemical synthesis. Across nearly all of these markets the bottleneck is the same: catalyst discovery and optimization remain slow, experimental and expensive, and the simulation tools available today answer narrower questions than the ones that actually decide a process. This is a once-in-a-career opportunity to shape a category-defining AI platform for materials science at the intersection of national security, scientific discovery, and commercial scale.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

- Own the end-to-end Catalysis product strategy, vision and roadmap, spanning CHIPS Act contractual deliverables, vertical scientific depth, and commercial expansion into new markets.

- Build a deep understanding of customer needs by working closely with Application Scientists and the Business Development team. Synthesize field insights, application benchmarking data, and market feedback into a clear picture of customer personas, and performance drivers, and translate these into prioritized product requirements and specifications.

- Translate the program's catalysis objectives into clear product requirements, a vertical roadmap, and the evidence packages required for Fulfillment Notices to the U.S. Department of Commerce.

- Define the dataset and model requirements for the vertical, chemical coverage, fidelity, and the benchmarking that determines where simulation investment is directed in partnership with our scientific and ML teams.

- Drive the roadmap from property and energetics prediction toward reaction-level modell

title: Mechanical Design Engineer
description:
Develop mechanical parts and complex assemblies in SolidWorks, from initial concepts through released designs. ● Produce clear, accurate engineering drawings, bills of materials, and specifications suitable for fabrication and assembly. ● Select appropriate materials, hardware, fits, and tolerances based on load, operating environment, manufacturing method, inspection requirements, and service conditions. ● Translate sometimes ambiguous engineering objectives into practical mechanical concepts and complete designs. ● Evaluate design trade-offs, document key assumptions, and make sound, defensible engineering decisions. ● Work directly with fabricators, suppliers, technicians, and production personnel throughout prototype and production builds. ● Support hands-on fit checks and integration activities on vessels and on the shop floor. ● Identify and resolve fit, manufacturability, fabrication, and assembly issues discovered during builds. ● Incorporate as-built feedback and maintain design revisions so released engineering information accurately reflects the product being built. ● Communicate technical progress, dependencies, design decisions, and risks clearly and early. ● Support continuous improvement of mechanical designs based on build, test, and operational feedback. Required Qualifications ● Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering. ● Approximately 3-6 years of relevant mechanical design experience. ● Strong hands-on experience with SolidWorks, including part modeling, complex or large assemblies, drawing creation, and design modifications. ● Practical knowledge of engineering drawings, dimensioning and tolerancing, materials, fasteners, machining, sheet metal, and general fabrication methods. ● Experience taking mechanical designs through prototype and/or production builds. ● Experience resolving real-world fit, fabrication, assembly, or manufacturability issues in collaboration with technicians or shop personnel. ● Ability to work effectively with limited oversight, take ownership of an objective, manage ambiguity, make reasoned engineering decisions, and deliver a complete design. ● Strong organizational skills, clear technical communication, and reliable follow-through. Preferred Experience ● Mechanical design experience within the marine or small-craft industry. ● Vessel integration or mechanical systems integration experience. ● Experience designing equipment for harsh or demanding operating environments. ● Understanding of corrosion-aware material selection. ● Practical familiarity with machining operations and fabrication processes. ● Experience working directly with technicians, machinists, welders, fabricators, or production teams. What Success Looks Like You are comfortable taking ownership of a mechanical design rather than working only on isolated CAD tasks. You can move from an engineering objective to a practical design, create fabrication-ready documentation, work directly with the people building the product, and make sensible engineering decisions when real-world build conditions require changes. You combine strong CAD capability with practical engineering judgment and understand that a successful design must work not only on screen, but also on the shop floor and in the field. Compensation The anticipated base salary range for this position is 60, 000-80,000 per year, depending on relevant experience, technical capability, and qualifications. Work Location This is an on-site position based at Marcurius headquarters in Clearwater, Florida. The role requires close collaboration with engineering and production teams and regular hands-on involvement with prototype and production builds

title: Financial Controller - Remote - Independent Contractor - PH Based
description:
Living in a Bubble sells premium campervan and outdoor accessories, direct to consumers and through marketplaces in Australia, the United States, Canada and Germany. We operate across two legal entities and five tax jurisdictions. We are a team of fourteen - two in Australia, twelve working remotely across the Philippines and elsewhere. We are small, run properly, and our bookkeeping is handled by an external firm. What we do not have is a finance professional who owns the output.
Right now the CEO does all of the finance: the monthly close, five indirect tax regimes, the pricing analysis, the landed cost, the advisor coordination. It works, and it does not scale, and there is no one else who could pick it up.
You would take that. Not the bookkeeping - an external firm does the bookkeeping. The layer above it: whether the numbers are right, whether the filings are on time, and whether someone other than the founder can read the business.
This is a build-and-run role in a business that has never had one. You will inherit real processes that mostly work and real gaps that do not. You bring the analysis and the judgement; the CEO keeps the final call on pricing, payments, tax and structure.
What you would own

•
The monthly close. You own the calendar, the quality bar and the query queue while the external bookkeeper does the execution. Settlement reconciliation for two marketplace accounts, the consolidated group P&L across both entities, the stock take, and the year-end pack for our Australian tax advisors. Getting the close to business day five is a first-half objective, not a week-one expectation.

•
Indirect tax in five jurisdictions. US sales tax, German VAT, UK VAT under Making Tax Digital, Canadian GST, Australian BAS. Four external firms do the filings. You are not expected to have technical depth in all five regimes - nobody does. You run the control that sits over them: a filing calendar nobody misses, data prepared to each firm's specification, a reconciliation of what was filed against what the books say, and a written query log when the two disagree.

•
Management reporting. Daily channel P&L across both marketplace accounts, a weekly sales report, a monthly P&L analysis with an executive summary someone acts on, the KPI scorecard, product and range performance. Today these exist in pieces; you would make them one thing.

•
Pricing and unit economics. The standing price review, margin verification after every price change, markdowns on aged stock, contribution by channel, third-party logistics cost against what we are charged. You bring the analysis; the CEO decides.

•
Landed cost. A monthly reference refresh and verification of cost uploads. Cost rolls forward in our systems, so an error corrupts forward margin silently and nothing tells you. There is a backlog of known cost conflicts to work through in your first half-year.

•
Controls and documentation. A written SOP for every recurring process, an access map so the function survives any one person being unavailable, and an audit-readiness file that does not exist today. These are gating deliverables, not nice-to-haves.

Not in this role
Payment release stays with the CEO. Accounts payable processing and payroll preparation stay where they are today, with our EA and the external bookkeeper, so your time goes to the close, the tax control, the reporting and the analysis. As the function grows, a finance assistant will take on that transactional layer and report to you.
Your first 90 days

•
Month 1. Access to everything, mapped and documented. Take over the daily and weekly reporting. Sit through one full close and write down what actually happens, as opposed to what is supposed to. Inherit the filing calendar and confirm two quarters of deadlines.

•
Month 2. Own the close on its current timetable, fully documented, and give us a dated plan to bring it forward to business day five. Produce the consolidated group P&L without the CEO involved. Run the landed-cost

The work we do with patients is hard enough and over the years we have found that our team often does their best work when the administrative burdens are taken off their plate and they are able to be fully present with their patients. Our administrative support team handles all non-clinical tasks so that you don’t have to think about anything except focusing on your patients.

Why bother with the endless administrative burdens and isolation of private practice? Use your highly trained interpersonal skills to change the culture around mental health care, decrease stigma, and help people who need you, while being supported by an experienced multi-disciplinary team of clinicians. Let us take care of the rest!

Want to work part time? No problem. Want to do group therapy? Sure! Want to do long-term psychodynamic psychotherapy with all of your clients? We do it every day. Interested in treating couples? title: Talent Acquisition Administrator
description:
Talent Acquisition Administrator
The Talent Acquisition Administrator provides administrative and systems support to the Talent Acquisition team, reporting to the Director, Talent Acquisition. This role owns the day-to-day upkeep of the applicant tracking system (ATS), keeps job requisitions accurate and current, and helps process employee job changes, including promotions, demotions, and transfers. The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, organized, and comfortable working with confidential information across HR systems.
Essential Duties & Responsibilities

• Maintain the applicant tracking system (ATS), including user access, job templates, workflows, candidate statuses, and system settings, in partnership with the Director, Talent Acquisition

• Audit open, on-hold, and filled requisitions on a regular cadence to ensure accurate status, approvals, hiring manager, recruiter assignment, and position details

• Open, update, and close job requisitions in the ATS according to approval workflows, and resolve duplicate, stale, or incomplete requisitions

• Reconcile ATS requisition data against HRIS and headcount/position records and flag discrepancies to Talent Acquisition and HR leadership

• Assist in processing employee job changes, including promotions, demotions, lateral moves, and transfers, by preparing documentation, routing approvals, and entering changes accurately and on time

• Coordinate with HR, Payroll, and hiring managers to confirm effective dates, compensation changes, and required paperwork for job changes

• Generate recurring and ad hoc ATS and requisition reports (e.g., open requisitions, time-to-fill, pipeline status) for the Talent Acquisition team and leadership

• Serve as a first point of contact for recruiter and hiring manager ATS questions; provide basic troubleshooting and training, and escalate system issues to the vendor as needed

• Maintain and document ATS and requisition procedures, data standards, and job aids

• Maintain confidentiality of candidate and employee information and ensure records comply with company policy and applicable recordkeeping requirements

• Understand and demonstrate safe work practices at all times to ensure a safe work environment

• Comply with all company policies and procedures

• Complete special projects and other duties as assigned by your supervisor
Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

• Strong attention to detail and accuracy in data entry, auditing, and recordkeeping

• Working knowledge of applicant tracking systems and HR information systems, with the ability to learn new platforms quickly

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel (sorting, filtering, lookups, and basic reporting)

• Strong organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines

• Clear written and verbal communication skills, with a customer-service mindset when supporting recruiters and hiring managers

• Ability to handle sensitive and confidential information with discretion

• Basic understanding of HR processes such as requisition approvals, job changes, and employee data management
Experience and Credentials

• High school diploma or equivalent required; Associate’s or Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field preferred

• 1-3 years of experience in an HR, recruiting, or administrative support role

• Hands-on experience using an applicant tracking system (e.g., Workday, iCIMS, Greenhouse, SuccessFactors, or similar) required. Experience in ADP Recruitment Manager and ADP Lyric highly preferred.

• Experience processing employee data changes in an HRIS preferred
Physical & Work Environment Requirements

• Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer.

• Ability to travel occasionally for meetings, training, or customer engagements.

title: Senior Applied Scientist - AI Platform
description:
AI Platform builds the foundations of Datadog's AI efforts. The org is 70+ people organised in three pillars: training and serving (GPU clusters, distributed training, low-level infrastructure), agents (agent harnesses, memory systems, the internal AI gateway that routes every LLM request at Datadog), and evaluation and experimentation. This role sits in the evaluation and experimentation pillar, which owns Datadog's shared annotation and evaluation infrastructure - including the evaluation scenario store and the telemetry archival systems used across the Bits org. Together they let an agent travel back in time and query what Datadog looked like at the exact moment an incident happened, so scenarios can be replayed and agent performance tracked over time.

Specifically, you'll be the first applied scientist on GenSim (Generative Simulations), the team that builds the environments Datadog's agents learn in. GenSim doesn't replay sampled telemetry - it stands up real, fully instrumented applications that talk to Datadog, drives them with representative traffic, injects controlled failures, and records what happens. Because GenSim injected the failure, it knows the ground truth. That corpus - hundreds of postmortem-derived scenarios and thousands of runnable applications - is today the primary source of post-training data for Datadog's own SRE model, and the substrate that Bits AI SRE and our other agents are trained and evaluated against.

The team has no applied science support today and is learning post-training data methodology on the fly. That's the gap this role fills, and the open questions are the interesting part. How do you tell whether a generated environment is actually representative of the messy, incomplete telemetry real customers run - rather than a suspiciously clean one where every monitor exists and every service emits complete logs? title: Head of Strategy & Global Expansion
description:
Thread Recruitment is proud to support Straightcurve in finding its Head of Strategy & Global Expansion. You’ll work alongside the founder as a strategic partner, own the group’s commercial performance, and turn ambitious ideas into clear decisions and results.
Straightcurve is a design-led landscape products business already selling in seven countries. Its products are proven, and its automated systems are designed to scale.
Now it’s looking to strengthen the markets it’s already in and build the ones that come next, starting with the USA.
Plenty of people can talk strategy. Very few can make it work. If you’re one of them, keep reading.
What You’ll Be Doing
This is strategy with its sleeves rolled up. You’ll work closely with Straightcurve’s founder to decide what deserves attention and turn the right opportunities into plans the team can deliver.
You’ll integrate the work across sales, operations, marketing and international markets. Strong leaders run each area independently; you’ll set direction with them, connect their work and keep the business moving in the same direction.
What that looks like in practice:

• Owning the group P&L and overseeing cash flow across the business

• Building the commercial case and action plan for new ideas, including the numbers, risks, people and practical steps needed to deliver

• Leading Straightcurve’s expansion into the USA

• Growing the UK business

• Scaling Australia, the engine of the business, while improving its profitability

• Spotting and validating the next market opportunity

• Deciding what to pursue now and what can wait, so the business stays focused

• Building the systems and structure that let each market run itself

The role is remote, but it isn’t hands-off. Expect to travel across Australia and overseas a few times a year, spending time on the ground with the people and the work that make Straightcurve run.
Who You Are
You’re a builder with a numbers brain. You’ve owned a P&L, you can read a balance sheet, and you’ve taken something from an idea to a trading business. You’d rather get on the ground and understand a market than theorise about it from a boardroom.
You’re calm under pressure and restless for what’s next. A good idea gets you moving; the numbers keep you honest. You challenge with evidence rather than ego, see the risks and find a way around them, and bring a team-first mindset to everything you do.
You’ll bring:

• Fluency with P&Ls, balance sheets, budgets and cash flow

• Proof you’ve built or scaled something: a business, a market or a team

• A systems mind: you see how the pieces connect and build structure that lasts

• The ability to lead strong, independent people without micromanaging them

• Comfort with ambiguity, backed by the judgement to know when to push and when to pause

• Curiosity about the world, and a drive to always find ways to make things better

• Permanent Australian work rights

Why Join Straightcurve?
Straightcurve is more than it looks. From the outside, it’s a landscape edging business with a serious commitment to sustainability. Inside, it’s a team that’s genuinely passionate about what they do, in a business built to put heart back into work. The people here care about building something bigger than themselves.
You can expect:

• A seat alongside the founder, with ownership of the numbers and the growth

• A direct impact on how the business grows

• Flexibility and autonomy of remote work, with time on the ground where it counts

• Freedom to make decisions, with accountability for what follows

• A team that works closely together and genuinely has each other’s back

• Room for the role to grow with the business

• A competitive salary plus super

Apply Now
You’ve built something before. This time, the foundations are already in place, and the opportunity is much bigger.
Send us your CV and a thoughtful cover letter or reach out to for a confidential conversation.

title: Certified Professional Coder- Orthopedic
description:

Job Summary:
The Certified Professional Coder performs various duties to accurately interpret and bill physician charges for physician services by entering into the appropriate CPT, ICD-10, and modifiers into the Billing system.

(This is a full-time hybrid or remote position that will support the RCM team, Monday to Friday 8 am to 5 pm- Coding certification required )

Primary Job Responsibilities/Tasks may include, but not limited to:

• Performs initial charge review to determine appropriate ICD-10 and CPT codes to be used to report physician services to third party payers.

• Interprets progress notes, operative reports, discharge summaries, and charge documents to determine services provided and accurately assign CPT and ICD-10 coding to these services, according to guidelines established by the AMA.

• Enter appropriate data into the TMP billing system by selecting the appropriate codes, diagnosis, modifiers, to complete the charge process.

• Adheres to department guidelines for timeliness of processing charges and communicates with team members and practice management on an ongoing basis to ensure these guidelines are met.

• Contacts physicians through query protocols regarding procedures and other services billed to ensure proper coding.

• A minimum of three (3) years’ experience with CPT and ICD-10 coding of physician services required.

• Coding certification required. CPC Certification preferred. Must maintain active certification and required CEUs during employment tenure.

• Advanced working knowledge of medical terminology, anatomy, and physiology required.

• Knowledge of and the ability to apply payer specific rules regarding coding, bundling, and adding appropriate modifiers.

• Understanding of and familiarity with regulatory guidelines including NCDs and LCDs.

Experience:

• Family Practice, Internal Medicine, Cardiology, Rheumatology, Endocrinology, Gynecology, and Dermatology preferred.

• Knowledge of current third-party billing and collection regulatory guidelines and requirements.

• Advanced knowledge of the ICD-10 CM/PCS and CPT/HCPCS coding systems and conventions.

• Advanced knowledge of, but not limited to, Official Coding Guidelines and methodologies.

• Knowledge of current third-party billing and collection regulatory guidelines and requirements.

• Good interpersonal skills and a basic understanding of team concept.

• Ability to gather and interpret clinical data.

• Ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment.

Physical Requirements:

• Work consistently requires walking, standing, sitting, lifting, reaching, stooping, bending, pushing, and pulling.

• Must be able to lift and support weight of 35 pounds.

• Ability to concentrate on details.

• Use of computer for long periods of time.

title: Senior Backend Engineer, Payments
description:
Brief info about Vinted 

Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life - or even a third.
The Vinted Group is made up of three business units that support this mission:

Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life.

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. 

Information about the position 

We’re looking for Senior Backend Engineers to join Vinted Payments Product - the financial product powering payments, payouts, balances and verification flows for millions of Vinted members.

Depending on your background and interests, you could join one of two teams:

- Verifications - the team building identity, eKYC and bank account verification systems behind Vinted Pay. Their work helps confirm that members are who they say they are, and that their bank account really belongs to them.

- Phoenix - the team building and scaling the core ledger systems at the heart of Vinted Pay. Their work ensures every money movement is recorded correctly and every balance is right.

Both teams work on business-critical, compliance-sensitive backend systems used at scale. We’re launching new markets, onboarding millions of members onto Vinted Pay, and building foundations that will support the platform for years to come.

In this position, you’ll 

• Work in a compact product-engineering team with backend engineers, an engineering manager, a product manager and a decision scientist.

• Build and operate backend services that directly support payments, payouts, verification, onboarding, balance activation and money movement across Vinted Pay.

• Own topics end-to-end: from an unclear requirement to a written technical proposal, cross-team alignment, implementation, rollout behind feature flags and monitoring in production.

• Improve and scale high-throughput services in Go, and connect them into reliable, always-on payment and verification flows.

• Build resilient integrations with third-party providers, including API clients, callbacks, durable workflows, dashboards, SLA alerts and vendor-facing debugging.

• Design systems that handle failure well: timeouts, provider outages, rate limits, retries, missing callbacks, inconsistent responses and data consistency issues.

• Work with distributed systems concepts such as idempotency, at-least-once delivery, workflow orchestration, provider routing and consistency across services.

• Handle sensitive financial and personal data responsibly, including PII tagging, log masking, retention and deletion requirements.

• Use AI-assisted engineering workflows with tools such as Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and others to build, debug, investigate production issues and write plans or documentation.

• See your code affect millions of members almost instantly. Our main branch is deployed straight to production on each merge, many times per day.

description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

As the Group grows, our GL organization is getting bigger and more complex. Local GL Managers stay responsible for their countries and teams. But some issues cut across borders or need extra experienced hands.

You'll step in on difficult finance issues, work out why they happened, and make sure each one ends with a lasting fix and a clear owner. You'll work directly with reconciliations, data and transactions when that's the fastest route to an answer.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Get hands-on: take ownership of selected accounting, reconciliation, close or process issues. Find the root cause and escalate material risks early.

- Strengthen GL quality: run sample reviews of reconciliations and key controls with local teams. Spread good practice and help set practical minimum standards.

- Improve processes: simplify and standardize GL processes across countries, while respecting real local needs.

- Lead cross-country projects: take on investigations that don't sit with one country team. Bring clear findings and recommendations, and see them through.

- Help GL scale: spot patterns behind recurring problems and help decide who should own the fix.

WHO YOU ARE

- You have solid experience in external audit, financial controlling, accounting or a similar finance role.

- You know GL accounting, balance sheets, month-end close and reconciliations well.

- You can trace reported balances back to transactions and documents.

- You're strong in Excel and data analysis, and comfortable with ERP systems.

- You've worked with many stakeholders without formal authority.

- You have professional-level English.

- Experience across several entities or countries is a plus.

You also bring:

- A hands-on, low-ego approach

- Curiosity, and a habit of asking why

- Independent judgement, and the courage to challenge constructively

- A root-cause mindset and a sense of materiality

- Comfort with ambiguity, and the follow-through to deliver

HOW THE ROLE WORKS

- You work with GL Managers, Financial Controllers and other Group Finance functions.
